Ready-made rules

Source: R/rul.R
ruleinset.Rd

The checks that account for most of what a table is asked: a value in a set, a number in a range, no missing value, no repeated identifier, a pattern, an order, an outlier, complete rows, distinct rows, a number of columns. Each returns a rule for valrules(), as rul() does.

Usage

ruleinset(col, set, napass = TRUE, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

rulebtw(col, lo, hi, napass = TRUE, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

rulenull(col, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

ruleuniq(col, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

rulerx(col, pat, napass = TRUE, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

ruleincr(col, strict = FALSE, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

rulemad(col, n = 3, napass = TRUE, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

rulecmpl(sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

ruledstn(cols = NULL, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

rulecolcnt(n, sev = c("warning", "fatal"))

Arguments

col

The column the rule reads: one non-empty string.

set

The allowed values.

napass

TRUE (the default) lets a missing value pass.

sev

"warning" (the default) or "fatal": how serious a failure is. valrules() records it; the caller decides what follows.

lo, hi

The bounds, both included.

pat

A regular expression.

strict

TRUE for strictly increasing.

n

rulemad(): the number of median absolute deviations allowed. rulecolcnt(): the number of columns.

cols

The columns over which rows must be distinct, or NULL (all of them).

Value

A rule: an object of class clrule, a list of rule (the kind), name, col (for a rule on one column), sev, msg and what the rule was given.

Details

ruleinset(): every value is one of set (compared as text). rulebtw(): every value lies in [lo, hi]. rulenull(): no value is missing. ruleuniq(): no value repeats; the rows reported are the repeats, not the first occurrence. rulerx(): every value matches the regular expression pat. ruleincr(): the column never falls (or, with strict, always rises) down the rows; missing values are passed over. rulemad(): every value lies within n median absolute deviations of the median, the deviation scaled by 1.4826 as stats::mad() scales it (so that it estimates the standard deviation of normal data; Leys et al. 2013 argue for this screen over one built on the mean and the standard deviation, which the outliers themselves inflate); when the deviation is 0 (more than half the values equal) any other value fails. rulecmpl(): no row has a missing value. ruledstn(): no row repeats, over all columns or over cols. rulecolcnt(): the table has n columns.

With napass = TRUE, the default, a missing value passes a rule about values (missingness is rulenull()'s question); with FALSE it fails. rulebtw(), ruleincr() and rulemad() read numbers (or dates, or TRUE and FALSE): on a column of text they are reported as rules that could not be evaluated, not passed.

A pattern is read by grepl() with perl = TRUE; the other languages of the package read it as ECMAScript, and the syntax the two share (classes, anchors, counts, alternation, groups) means the same in both. A pattern is at most 256 bytes, and a value it is tried on at most 4096.

Errors: col not one non-empty string; lo or hi not one number, or lo above hi; n not one positive number (rulecolcnt(): one whole number of at least 0); pat not one string of at most 256 bytes, or not a regular expression; cols neither NULL nor column names; sev not "warning" or "fatal".

References

Leys, C., Ley, C., Klein, O., Bernard, P. and Licata, L. (2013). Detecting outliers: do not use standard deviation around the mean, use absolute deviation around the median. Journal of Experimental Social Psychology, 49(4), 764-766. doi:10.1016/j.jesp.2013.03.013

Hampel, F. R. (1974). The influence curve and its role in robust estimation. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 69(346), 383-393. doi:10.1080/01621459.1974.10482962

See also

rul() and valrules().

Examples

d <- data.frame(year = c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2021),
                n = c(410, 395, 9000, 402),
                div = c("11", "14", "14", "5X"))
valrules(d, list(
  rulebtw("year", 2000, 2026),
  ruleincr("year", strict = TRUE),
  rulemad("n", 5),
  rulerx("div", "^[0-9]{2}$"),
  ruledstn(c("year", "div")),
  rulecolcnt(3),
  rulecmpl()
))
#> valrules: 7 rules, 3 failed (0 fatal)
#>   warning  year_increasing: Column 'year' is not strictly increasing
#>   warning  n_within_mads: Column 'n' has values more than 5 MADs from its median (1 of 4 rows); rows 3
#>   warning  div_regex: Column 'div' has values not matching /^[0-9]{2}$/ (1 of 4 rows); rows 4
try(rulebtw("year", 2026, 2000))
#> Error : rulebtw: `lo` must not be above `hi`.
